mechanism_narrative: A low and stable unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a strong labor market, which positively impacts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following low UNRATE, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) crosses above 5%, it indicates monetary tightening, which can lead to decreased corporate borrowing and investment, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 35% of the 20-day windows after FEDFUNDS exceeds 5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Rising consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) coupled with increasing federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS) indicates a tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases by 0.5% and FEDFUNDS increases by 0.25%
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 30% of the 60-day windows following the trigger, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: During a late-cycle expansion, an increase in housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong demand in the housing market, which can lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 60-day windows following increased HOUST, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates a strong supply chain and manufacturing sector, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 35% of the 20-day windows following increased INDPRO, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates a strong labor market, which can lead to increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 30% of the 5-day windows following the trigger, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A strong GDP growth (GDPC1) coupled with a high unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates an imbalanced economic expansion, which can lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases by 0.5% and UNRATE remains above 4.5%
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 35% of the 60-day windows following the trigger, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: During an early-cycle recovery, an increase in retail sales (RSAFS) indicates consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following increased RSAFS, the hypothesis is rejected.
